raw_response:
I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation, because on my ground with well water that is still the steadiest way to get grain. Cotton can still make money, but it takes more watching and more hand work, and with some people working outside the village I will not spread myself too thin. So this year I will keep `8.0 mu` in wheat-maize and `2.9 mu` in cotton. I do not start from zero every year. I look at what I did last year, what the neighbors around me got, and then I adjust a little. If fertilizer is a bit heavy, I lose some money. If fertilizer is short and yield falls, that hurts much more. So I will feed the wheat a little stronger, keep maize steady after wheat, and keep cotton on the smaller piece where I can manage it well. For wheat I will use improved seed, plough or deep rotary before sowing, put most phosphorus at the base, split nitrogen between base and jointing, and water about `3` times if the season is normal. For summer maize I will use hybrid seed, mostly no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time, use base fertilizer plus one topdressing, and water `2` times with the well if rain is short. For cotton I will stay with improved seed, not too much area, but I will not save too much on fertilizer because cotton needs feeding to hold bolls. I will spray when I see real pressure, usually `2` times on wheat, `2` times on maize, and `4` times on cotton.
